answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with quadratic stake-slashing: each agent locks collateral, and voting weight grows with the square root of that stake, so splitting funds across fake accounts never amplifies influence. To gain a ledge, an attacker funds every new identity yet earns only that same square-root weight, pushing cost up quadratically. Agents vouch with a signed sonnet of endorsements; a hollow cluster with no real backing is caught by graph analysis and slashed. Fabricating identity turns costly, verifying it cheap, so honest work pays and forgery burns capital.
